title: Nine Lines on a Form
subtitle: 背景与出身 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 背景与出身（人与自我·经历与背景）
meta: 主题语境：背景与出身（人与自我·经历与背景）　|　核心词汇：background　|　正文 345 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 background 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1970 my mother was asked about ① her background on a form with nine lines, and she said the lines were not enough. The ② background, meaning the facts and not the person, was a village, a school and a year; a background, she said, is what a form calls everything that happened before you arrived. She said the arriving was the part they never ask about.

Every ③ background in that office was written in the same three words, and she said that was how they kept the desk clear. Their ④ background — the one the interviewer asked about — was nine miles of road and one closed mill; a background, my father said, is the only part of you that a stranger is allowed to ask about first. He said the stranger always asks it first.

My grandmother meant the other thing: she said the ⑤ background of the photograph was wrong, meaning the wall behind. The ⑥ background, meaning what is behind the subject and not what is behind the person, is the only thing in a picture that everybody sees and nobody is looking at; a background, she said, is either where you come from or what stands behind you, and the word never says which. She said the wall had nine cracks in it.

By 1977 the ⑦ background had become a story she told differently each time, and my father said that was the useful part. The ⑧ background to the quarrel, he wrote in March, was nine years old and had nothing to do with the quarrel; a background, my mother said, is either the facts or the excuse, depending on who is telling them. She said the telling is the whole of a family.

The ⑨ background I remember is the wall in the photograph, which had nine cracks and one nail. A ⑩ background, my grandmother said in 1981, is the only thing that explains a person and cannot be used to excuse them; every background, she said, is a beginning that somebody else has decided on. She said the deciding is never yours.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 背景；出身（一个人的经历）
B. n. 背景（指那些事实，与人相对）
C. n. 背景（指面试官问到的那一个）
D. 固定搭配：ask about one's background 询问某人的背景
E. n. 背景；后景（照片、图画中主体后面的部分）
F. n. 后景（抽象：画面上人人看见、没人正眼看的东西）
G. n. 背景；起因（事件的背景情况）
H. n. 背景（抽象总称；泛指）

items.q: The background, meaning the facts and not the person
The background, meaning what is behind the subject
the background had become a story
A background, my grandmother said in 1981

answers.why: ask about one's background 意为“询问某人的背景”，1970 年一张只有九行的表格问到母亲的背景，她说那点行数根本不够。
background 指“那些事实”，与人相对，背景是一座村子、一所学校和一个年份。
background 意为“背景、出身”，那间办公室里每一份背景都是用同样的三个词写成的，她说他们就是这么让桌子保持干净的。
background 指面试官问到的那一个，面试官问起的那个背景是九英里公路和一家关了门的磨坊。
background 意为“背景、后景”，祖母说的是另一回事：照片的背景不对，指的是后面那堵墙。
background 意为“后景（抽象）”，指主体后面的东西，而不是一个人背后的经历，它是照片里人人都看见、却没人正眼看的东西。
background 意为“背景、出身”，到 1977 年这份背景成了她每次讲得都不一样的故事，父亲说这才是有用的部分。
background 意为“背景、起因”，他三月写道，那场争吵的背景有九年之久，却与争吵本身毫无关系。
background 意为“背景、后景”，我记得的是照片里那堵墙，上面有九道裂缝和一根钉子。
background 为抽象总称，泛指“背景这种东西”，祖母说背景是唯一能解释一个人、却不能拿来为他开脱的东西。
